* WHERE...Western Clay County in northeastern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 1100 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin

between 2 and 6 inches. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...Portions of central and south central Montana.

* WHEN...From midnight Saturday Night to noon MDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult, due to areas of slushy or

properties.description:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts of 35 to 50 mph
expected over higher terrain above 1,500 feet and in the valleys
immediately northwest of the Pine, Black, Cumberland, and Log
Mountains. Communities at greatest risk for the strongest wind
gusts include Cumberland, Eolia, Chenoa, Frakes, and Mayking.

should expect southeast winds of 10 to 15 mph with occasional gusts

* WHEN...From noon Saturday to 5 AM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs and weakly rooted trees in steep terrain could be blown down
and a few power outages may result.

profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 9 at 8:53PM EDT until October 9 at 10:00PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
SMWJAX

The National Weather Service in Jacksonville has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine FL out 20
NM...

* Until 1000 PM EDT.

* At 853 PM EDT, a shower producing waterspouts was located 13 nm
east of Palm Valley, or 21 nm northeast of Saint Augustine, moving
north at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can create locally hazardous seas. Small
craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* The shower will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally hazardous
seas. Seek safe harbor immediately. If your vessel is caught
offshore, immediately secure for heavy weather. Ensure all crew
members are wearing USCG approved Type I life jackets and
nonessential crew are below decks. Deploy jack lines and harnesses if
available. Check life saving equipment, including batteries on
handheld radios, for readiness.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 9 at 8:52PM EDT by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
A period of strong wind gusts is expected on Saturday as the
remnants of Hurricane Isaias move into eastern Kentucky.
Southeasterly winds of 10 to 20 mph, with gusts up to 35 mph are
expected. The strongest winds are expected during the afternoon
and should coincide with the arrival of the leading bands of rain.
Once rainfall becomes steady, many areas will see the winds
lighten, except at elevations above 1,500 feet, where the gusty
winds are expected to continue into Saturday night. Isolated gusts
over 40 mph are possible over the highest ridge tops. The gusty
winds could blow around unsecured outdoor objects and decor.

NWSheadline: Gusty Winds Expected Saturday and Saturday night with the Remnants of Hurricane Isaias

properties.description:

exercise caution when traveling. If a road way is flooded, remember
"Turn Around, Don't Drown!".

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Guam.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

today. Invest 95W continues to linger just off the east coast of
Guam and is producing heavy rainfall over the island. Additional
heavy rainfall will likely lead to flash flooding due to the
saturated conditions.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 9 at 8:46PM EDT until October 10 at 5:36PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

Cypress Creek At SR 54 Worthington Gardens affecting Pasco County.

Anclote River At Elfers at Little Road affecting Pasco County.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Little Manatee River At Wimauma at US 301 affecting Hillsborough
County.

Manatee River Near Myakka Head at SR 64 affecting Manatee County.

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Levy and Citrus
Counties.

.Due to recent heavy rainfall, water levels on Anclote River and
Manatee River are forecast to remain at flood stage and begin to fall
Saturday. Water levels on the Cypress Creek and Little Manatee River
are expected to continue rising and reach Flood Stage during the
weekend or early in the week.

Elevated water levels continue on the Withlacoochee River at
Dunnellon due to a combination of excessive hydrilla growth along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between U.S. 41 and Lake Rousseau, and
recent heavy rainfall. Water levels are expected to hold steady
before slowly decreasing over the next several days. However, the
river is forecast to remain in flood stage.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring forecast to continue.

* WHERE...Anclote River at Elfers at Little Road.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 9 at 8:37PM EDT until October 9 at 11:30PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
FFWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Holmes County in the panhandle of Florida...
Central Walton County in the panhandle of Florida...

* Until 1030 PM CDT.

* At 737 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
De Funiak Springs, Eglin Air Force Base, Freeport, Ponce De Leon,
Rock Hill, New Home, Pleasant Ridge, Eucheeanna, De Funiak Spring
Airport, Portland, Alpine Heights, Argyle, Oakwood Hills, Douglass
Crossroad, Knox Hill, Red Bay, Mossy Head and Villa Tasso.

Very heavy rainfall from the eyewall of Hurricane Isaias is likely
producing flash flooding with repeated bands of additional rain.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
